questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The workdone in an adiabatic change in an ideal gas depends upon only :
questions.solution: Work done in adiabatic process = $\frac{nR\Delta T}{1 - \gamma}$. So, depends upon change in temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two projectiles are fired with same initial speed from same point on ground at angles of $(45^\circ - \alpha)$ and $(45^\circ + \alpha)$, respectively, with the horizontal direction. The ratio of their maximum heights attained is :
questions.solution: $H_{\max} = \frac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$. $\frac{H_1}{H_2} = \frac{\sin^2(45^\circ - \alpha)}{\sin^2(45^\circ + \alpha)} = \frac{(\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha)^2}{(\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha)^2} = \frac{1 - \sin 2\alpha}{1 + \sin 2\alpha}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Consider a long straight wire of a circular cross-section (radius $a$) carrying a steady current $I$. The current is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. The distances from the centre of the wire's cross-section at which the magnetic field [inside the wire, outside the wire] is half of the maximum possible magnetic field, anywhere due to the wire, will be
questions.solution: Magnetic field inside cylinder at distance $r_1$ from axis: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{\pi R^2} \cdot \frac{r_1}{2}$. $B_{\max} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi R}$. Setting $B = \frac{1}{2} B_{\max} \Rightarrow r_1 = \frac{R}{2} = \frac{a}{2}$. Magnetic field outside cylinder: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r_2} = \frac{1}{2} \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi R} \Rightarrow r_2 = 2R = 2a$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: At the interface between two materials having refractive indices $n_1$ and $n_2$, the critical angle for reflection of an em wave is $\theta_{1c}$. The $n_2$ material is replaced by another material having refractive index $n_3$ such that the critical angle at the interface between $n_1$ and $n_3$ materials is $\theta_{2c}$. If $n_3 > n_2 > n_1$; $\frac{n_2}{n_3} = \frac{2}{5}$ and $\sin \theta_{2c} - \sin \theta_{1c} = \frac{1}{2}$, then $\theta_{1c}$ is
questions.solution: Critical angle $\sin \theta_{1c} = \frac{n_1}{n_2}$ and $\sin \theta_{2c} = \frac{n_1}{n_3}$. Given $\frac{n_2}{n_3} = \frac{2}{5}$ and $\sin \theta_{2c} - \sin \theta_{1c} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Let $u$ and $v$ be the distances of the object and the image from a lens of focal length $f$. The correct graphical representation of $u$ and $v$ for a convex lens when $|u| > f$, is
questions.solution:
Lens formula $\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$
$$\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{u}$$
Since $|u| > f$, RHS is positive.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Choke coil is simply a coil having a large inductance but a small resistance. Choke coils are used with fluorescent mercury-tube fittings. If household electric power is directly connected to a mercury tube, the tube will be damaged.
Reason (R) : By using the choke coil, the voltage across the tube is reduced by a factor $\left( R / \sqrt{R^2 + \omega^2 L^2} \right)$, where $\omega$ is frequency of the supply across resistor $R$ and inductor $L$. If the choke coil were not used, the voltage across the resistor would be the same as the applied voltage.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
$I = \frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2 + \omega^2 L^2}}$
$V_R = \frac{R}{\sqrt{R^2 + \omega^2 L^2}} V$

questions.solution:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Consider $I_1$ and $I_2$ are the currents flowing simultaneously in two nearby coils $1$ & $2$, respectively. If $L_1 = \text{self inductance of coil } 1$, $M_{12} = \text{mutual inductance of coil } 1 \text{ with respect to coil } 2$, then the value of induced emf in coil 1 will be
questions.solution:
Magnitude of induced emf due to self inductance $= \frac{L_1 dI_1}{dt}$
Magnitude of induced emf due to mutual inductance $= \frac{M_{12} dI_2}{dt}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An electric dipole of mass $m$, charge $q$, and length $l$ is placed in a uniform electric field $\vec{E} = E_0 \hat{i}$. When the dipole is rotated slightly from its equilibrium position and released, the time period of its oscillations will be :
questions.solution:
$\tau = PE_0 \sin\theta$
If $\theta$ is small
$\tau = -(PE_0)\theta$
$I = m\left(\frac{l}{2}\right)^2 \cdot 2 = \frac{ml^2}{2}$
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{ml^2}{2 \cdot PE_0}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{ml^2}{2 \cdot qlE_0}}$
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{ml}{2qE_0}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: As shown below, bob $A$ of a pendulum having massless string of length '$R$' is released from $60^\circ$ to the vertical. It hits another bob $B$ of half the mass that is at rest on a frictionless table in the center. Assuming elastic collision, the magnitude of the velocity of bob $A$ after the collision will be (take $g$ as acceleration due to gravity.)
questions.solution:
Velocity of $A$ before collision $= \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2g \times \frac{R}{2}} = \sqrt{Rg}$
After collision $v_1 \leftarrow \bullet_{m/2} \quad \bullet_m \rightarrow v_2$
COM
$mu = \frac{m}{2}v_1 + mv_2$
$2u = v_1 + 2v_2 \quad \dots(i)$
$e = 1, u = v_1 - v_2 \quad \dots(ii)$
$u = 3v_2$
$v_2 = \frac{u}{3} = \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{Rg}$

questions.text:
Match **List-I** with **List-II**.

$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|} \hline & \text{List-I} & & \text{List-II} \\ \hline (A) & \text{Electric field inside (distance } r > 0 \text{ from center) of a uniformly charged spherical shell with surface charge density } \sigma, \text{ and radius } R. & (I) & \sigma / \varepsilon_0 \\ \hline (B) & \text{Electric field at distance } r > 0 \text{ from a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet with surface charge density } \sigma. & (II) & \sigma / 2\varepsilon_0 \\ \hline (C) & \text{Electric field outside (distance } r > 0 \text{ from center) of a uniformly charged spherical shell with surface charge density } \sigma, \text{ and radius } R. & (III) & 0 \\ \hline (D) & \text{Electric field between } 2 \text{ oppositely charged infinite plane parallel sheets with uniform surface charge density } \sigma. & (IV) & \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0 r^2} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Inside uniformly charged spherical shell, $E = 0$
$\therefore A \rightarrow \text{III}$
For uniformly charged infinite plate $E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}$
$B \rightarrow \text{II}$
Outside of spherical shell $E = \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2} = \frac{\sigma R^2}{\varepsilon_0 r^2}$
None of the option is matching for $C$.
Between two plates $E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}$
$D \rightarrow \text{I}$
None of the option is correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
The fractional compression $\left(\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right)$ of water at the depth of $2.5\text{ km}$ below the sea level is ______ $\%$.
Given, the Bulk modulus of water $= 2 \times 10^9\text{ Nm}^{-2}$, density of water $= 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}$, acceleration due to gravity $= g = 10\text{ ms}^{-2}$.
questions.solution:
$B = \frac{\Delta P}{-\left(\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right)}$
$-\left(\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right) = \frac{\Delta P}{B} = \frac{\rho g h}{B} = \frac{10^3 \times 10 \times 2.5 \times 10^3}{2 \times 10^9} = 1.25\%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A coil of area $A$ and $N$ turns is rotating with angular velocity $\omega$ in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ about an axis perpendicular to $\vec{B}$. Magnetic flux $\varphi$ and induced emf $\varepsilon$ across it, at an instant when $\vec{B}$ is parallel to the plane of coil, are :
questions.solution:
$\phi = NBA \cos\theta$
$\varepsilon = -\frac{d\phi}{dt} = -NBA \frac{d\cos\theta}{dt}$
$\theta = \omega t$
$\varepsilon = -NBA\omega \sin\omega t$
if $B$ is parallel to plane of coil
$\theta = 90^\circ$
$\phi = 0, E = BA\omega N$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A body of mass '$m$' connected to a massless and unstretchable string goes in verticle circle of radius '$R$' under gravity $g$. The other end of the string is fixed at the center of circle. If velocity at top of circular path is $n\sqrt{gR}$, where $n \ge 1$, then ratio of kinetic energy of the body at bottom to that at top of the circle is
questions.solution:
$v = n\sqrt{gR}$
$v_0 = \sqrt{v^2 + 2g(2R)}$
$v_0 = \sqrt{n^2gR + 4gR}$
$\therefore \frac{k_{\text{bottom}}}{k_{\text{top}}} = \frac{v_0^2}{v^2} = \frac{n^2 + 4}{n^2}$

questions.text: Two light beams fall on a transparent material block at point 1 and 2 with angle $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$, respectively, as shown in figure. After refraction, the beams intersect at point 3 which is exactly on the interface at other end of the block. Given : the distance between 1 and 2, $d = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$ and $\theta_1 = \theta_2 = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{n_2}{2n_1}\right)$, where refractive index of the block $n_2 >$ refractive index of the outside medium $n_1$, then the thickness of the block is ________ cm.

$n_1 \sin(90^\circ - \theta_1) = n_2 \sin r$

A man in the boat throws a ball vertically upwards with speed of $10\text{ m/s}$. Range of the ball as observed by an observer at rest on the river bank, is ______ $\text{cm}$. questions.solution: $v_y = 10\text{ m/s}\nv_x = v_{\text{river}} + v_{\text{boat}} = 27 + 9 = 36\text{ km/h} = 10\text{ m/s}\nR = \left(\frac{2v_y}{g}\right)v_x = \frac{2 \times 10 \times 10}{10} = 20\text{ m} = 2000\text{ cm}$

options: $\text{AX}_2$ is fully ionised while $\text{AY}_2$ is completely unionised

questions.solution:

For $	ext{AY}_2$:
$\Delta T_b = i K_b m
0.0260 = i 	imes 0.52 	imes  rac{25.4}{250 	imes 2} \implies i \approx 1$

questions.text: At temperature $\text{T}$, compound $\text{AB}_2(\text{g})$ dissociates as $\text{AB}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{AB}(\text{g}) + \frac{1}{2}\text{B}_2(\text{g})$ having degree of dissociation $x$ (small compared to unity). $	ext{AB}_2(	ext{g}) ightleftharpoons 	ext{AB}(	ext{g}) +  rac{1}{2}	ext{B}_2(	ext{g})$
At $t=0$: $p_0$, $0$, $0$
At equilibrium: $p_0(1-x)$, $p_0 x$, $ rac{p_0 x}{2}$
$p = p_0 - p_0 x + p_0 x +  rac{p_0 x}{2} = p_0\left(1 +  rac{x}{2}ight)$
$p_0 =  rac{p}{1 +  rac{x}{2}}$
$	ext{K}_p =  rac{(p_{	ext{AB}})(p_{	ext{B}_2})^{1/2}}{(p_{	ext{AB}_2})} =  rac{(p_0 x)\left( rac{p_0 x}{2}ight)^{1/2}}{p_0(1-x)}$

questions.text:
Choose the correct statements :
(A) Weight of a substance is the amount of matter present in it.
(B) Mass is the force exerted by gravity on an object.
(C) Volume is the amount of space occupied by a substance.
(D) Temperatures below $0^\circ	ext{C}$ are possible in Celsius scale, but in Kelvin scale negative temperature is not possible.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Carbohydrate): (A) Amylose (B) Cellulose (C) Glycogen (D) Amylopectin. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: If $a_0$ is denoted as the Bohr radius of hydrogen atom, then what is the de-Broglie wavelength ($\lambda$) of the electron present in the second orbit of hydrogen atom? [$n$ : any integer]
questions.solution: $r_n = \frac{a_0 n^2}{z}$. Also, $2\pi r_n = n\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is de-Broglie wavelength. $\frac{2\pi a_0 n^2}{z} = n\lambda$. For second orbit of H-atom, $\lambda = \frac{8\pi a_0}{n}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The correct increasing order of stability of the complexes based on $\Delta_0$ value is: I. $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ II. $[\text{Co(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ III. $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ IV. $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$
questions.solution: Neglecting pairing energy: I. $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-} \Rightarrow \text{Mn}^{3+}, \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^4, \text{CFSE} = -0.4 \times 4 \Delta_0 = -1.6\Delta_0$. II. $[\text{Co(CN)}_6]^{4-} \Rightarrow \text{Co}^{2+}, \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^6 \text{e}_{\text{g}}^1, \text{CFSE} = -0.4 \times 6 + 0.6 \times 1 = -1.8\Delta_0$. III. $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-} \Rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}, \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^6 \text{e}_{\text{g}}^0, \text{CFSE} = -0.4 \times 6 = -2.4\Delta_0$. IV. $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-} \Rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+}, \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^5 \text{e}_{\text{g}}^0, \text{CFSE} = -0.4 \times 5 = -2\Delta_0$. Order of stability $\text{III} > \text{IV} > \text{II} > \text{I}$.

**Statement (II) :** The magnitude of electron gain enthalpy of halogen decreases in the order.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Define a relation $R$ on the interval $\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ by $x R y$ if and only if $\sec^2 x - \tan^2 y = 1$. Then $R$ is:
options: both reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
reflexive but neither symmetric not transitive
both reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
questions.solution:
$x R y : \sec^2 x - \tan^2 y = 1$

Check reflexive:
$x R x = \sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1$
$\forall x \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Check symmetric:
$x R y \Rightarrow y R x$
$\sec^2 x - \tan^2 y = 1$
$= \sec^2 y - \tan^2 x = (1 + \tan^2 y) - (\sec^2 x - 1)$
$= 2 - (\sec^2 x - \tan^2 y)$
$= 2 - 1 = 1$
$\Rightarrow y R x$

Check transitive:
$x R y$ and $y R z$
$\Rightarrow \sec^2 x - \tan^2 y = 1$
$\sec^2 y - \tan^2 z = 1$
Add $\Rightarrow \sec^2 x - \tan^2 z + (\sec^2 y - \tan^2 y) = 2$
$\Rightarrow \sec^2 x - \tan^2 z + 1 = 2 \Rightarrow x R z$
$\Rightarrow R$ is an equivalence relation.

$\frac{x - \frac{17}{3}}{2} = \frac{y - \frac{28}{3}}{6} = \frac{-2\left(2\left(\frac{17}{3}\right) + 6\left(\frac{28}{3}\right) - 53\right)}{2^2 + 6^2}$
$\Rightarrow h = 3, k = 4$

$\vec{a} \times \vec{c} = \vec{c} \times \vec{b} = -(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$

$\Rightarrow \vec{c}$ is parallel to $\vec{a} + \vec{b}$.
$\vec{c} = \lambda(5\hat{i} + (-6)\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) \Rightarrow |\vec{c}|^2 = \lambda^2(77)$
$(\vec{a} + \vec{c}) \cdot (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) = \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + |\vec{c}|^2 + \vec{c} \cdot (\vec{a} + \vec{b})$

$\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|^2 + \lambda(77) = 154$
$\Rightarrow 77\lambda^2 + 77\lambda - 152 = 0$
$\Rightarrow \lambda^2 + \lambda - 2 = 0$
$\Rightarrow (\lambda + 2)(\lambda - 1) = 0$
$|\vec{c}|^2_{\text{max}} = (-2)^2(77) = 308$

$\text{I.F.} = e^{-\int \frac{3 \tan x}{\ln \cos x} dx}$
Let $\ln \cos x = t$
$-\tan x \, dx = dt$
$e^{3\int \frac{dt}{t}} = e^{3\ln t} = t^3 = (\ln \cos x)^3$
$\therefore$ Solution will be
$y (\ln \cos x)^3 = -\int (\tan x)(\ln \cos x) dx$
$y (\ln \cos x)^3 = \frac{(\ln \cos x)^2}{2} + c$
$\because y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = -\frac{1}{\ln 2}$
$\Rightarrow c = 0$
$\therefore y = \frac{1}{2(\ln \cos x)}$
$y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{\ln \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)} = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{\ln \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)} = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{\ln \sqrt{3} - \ln 2} = \frac{1}{\ln 3 - \ln 4}$

questions.solution:
$I = \int_0^{\pi/4} \frac{\sin\theta + \cos\theta}{9 - 16\sin 2\theta} d\theta$
Take $\sin\theta - \cos\theta = t$

$(\sin\theta - \cos\theta)^2 = t^2 \Rightarrow \sin 2\theta = 1 - t^2$
$\theta = 0 \to t = -1$

$I = \int_{-1}^0 \frac{dt}{9 + 16(1 - t^2)} = \frac{1}{16} \int_{-1}^0 \frac{dt}{\frac{25}{16} - t^2} = \frac{1}{4} \left[ \frac{1}{10} \log \left| \frac{5 + 4t}{5 - 4t} \right| \right]_{-1}^0 = \frac{1}{40} [0 + \log_e 9]$

Given, $\int_0^1 f(\lambda x) d\lambda = a f(x)$ ...(1)
Let $\lambda x = u \Rightarrow d\lambda = \frac{1}{x} du$
$\therefore$ From (1), $\frac{1}{x} \int_0^x f(u) du = a f(x) \Rightarrow \int_0^x f(u) du = a x f(x)$
Differentiate both sides:
$f(x) = a (x f'(x) + f(x))$
$\Rightarrow f(x) = a x f'(x) + a f(x)$
$\Rightarrow (1 - a) f(x) = a x f'(x)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)} = \frac{(1 - a)}{a} \cdot \frac{1}{x}$
Integrate both sides w.r.t. $x$:
$\Rightarrow \int \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)} dx = \frac{(1 - a)}{a} \int \frac{1}{x} dx$
$\Rightarrow \ln f(x) = \left(\frac{1 - a}{a}\right) \ln x + c$
Now at $x = 1$, $f(1) = 1 \Rightarrow c = 0$
Also given $f(16) = \frac{1}{8}$
$\therefore \frac{1}{8} = (16)^{\frac{1-a}{a}} \Rightarrow 2^{-3} = 2^{\frac{4-4a}{a}} \Rightarrow -3 = \frac{4 - 4a}{a} \Rightarrow -3a = 4 - 4a \Rightarrow a = 4$
$\therefore f(x) = x^{-3/4}$
$f'(x) = -\frac{3}{4} x^{-\frac{7}{4}}$
Put $x = \frac{1}{16}$:
$f'\left(\frac{1}{16}\right) = -\frac{3}{4} \left(\frac{1}{16}\right)^{-7/4} = -\frac{3}{4} \cdot 2^7 = -96$
$\therefore 16 - f'\left(\frac{1}{16}\right) = 16 - (-96) = 112$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $S = \{x : \cos^{-1} x = \pi + \sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1}(2x + 1)\}$. Then $\sum_{x \in S} (2x - 1)^2$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution: $\cos^{-1} x = \pi + \sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1}(2x + 1)$ $\Rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1} x = \pi + \sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1}(2x + 1)$ $\Rightarrow -\frac{\pi}{2} - 2\sin^{-1} x = \sin^{-1}(2x + 1)$ $\Rightarrow \sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{2} - 2\sin^{-1} x\right) = \sin(\sin^{-1}(2x + 1))$ $\Rightarrow -\cos(2\sin^{-1} x) = (2x + 1)$ $\Rightarrow -(1 - 2x^2) = 2x + 1$ $\Rightarrow 2x^2 - 2x - 2 = 0$ $\Rightarrow x = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 + 16}}{4} = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$. Since $x = \frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$ is rejected, we have $x = \frac{1 - \sqrt{5}}{2}$. So, $\sum_{x \in S} (2x - 1)^2 = 5$.

questions.text: The number of 6-letter words, with or without meaning, that can be formed using the letters of the word MATHS such that any letter that appears in the word must appear at least twice is
questions.solution: Case 1: 3 letters repeated 2 times each = ${}^5C_3 \times \frac{6!}{2!2!2!} = 10 \times 90 = 900$. Case 2: 1 letter repeated 4 times & 1 letter repeated 2 times OR 2 letters repeated 3 times each = ${}^5C_2 \left( \frac{6!}{2!4!} \times 2 + \frac{6!}{3!3!} \right) = 10(15 \times 2 + 20) = 500$. Case 3: 1 letter repeated 6 times = ${}^5C_1 \cdot 1 = 5$. Total = $900 + 500 + 5 = 1405$.

questions.text: Let $S = \left\{ m \in \mathbf{Z} : A^{m^2} + A^m = 3I - A^{-6} \right\}$, where $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$. Then $n(S)$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution: Characteristic equation of $A$: $|A - \lambda I| = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda^2 - 2\lambda + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow (\lambda - 1)^2 = 0$. Since $A$ satisfies $(A - I)^2 = 0$, $A = I + N$ where $N = A - I = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $N^2 = 0$. Thus $A^m = I + mN$. Given condition gives $(m^2 + m)N = 6N$. Since $N \neq 0$, $m^2 + m - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow (m - 2)(m + 3) = 0 \Rightarrow m = 2, -3$. Number of elements in $S$ is 2.
